imp.generic: The big house was on the nice part of the street and had lots of lights on at night.
imp.author: The Hadley house stood at the high end of the avenue, white and indifferent behind its rows of clipped privet, and on summer nights it shed light the way a careless woman sheds compliments.

imp.generic: She was friendly to everyone who showed up, even though she didn't really care about most of them.
imp.author: She had the particular gift of making each arrival feel like the one she had been waiting for all evening; it was a lie, of course, but a generous lie, the kind that costs the teller nothing and warms the listener for a week.

imp.generic: I had a crush on her for years but never did anything about it.
imp.author: I had loved her in a thin, hopeful way for three years, the way a poor man loves a house he passes on his walk home, and I had told myself that nearness would be enough. It is never enough.

imp.generic: He came back from Europe acting rich and showing off, but he seemed unhappy underneath.
imp.author: Now he dined everywhere, signed everything, and laughed too quickly at his own remarks, and underneath it I heard the small dry rattle of a man who has discovered that the moon, once reached, is only cold stone after all.

imp.generic: Once you get everything you want, life feels empty.
imp.author: The trouble with getting everything you wanted is that it leaves you nothing to want, and a man without wanting is a clock without hands, beautiful and useless and exactly on time for nothing.

imp.generic: She was pretty and turned down a lot of guys when she was young, but later she ran out of options.
imp.author: Beauty, I have come to think, is a kind of credit extended by the young against a future they assume will pay; June had spent hers freely, magnificently, on nothing in particular, and now the account was closing in the slow polite way that accounts do.

imp.generic: It was the end-of-summer party and everyone was tired but trying to have fun.
imp.author: By then the summer people were tired in the way that pleasure makes you tired, hollowed and luminous, and they came to dance the final dances with a desperate gaiety that fooled no one and comforted everyone.

imp.generic: The old rich man said the music reminded him of his youth and that made him sad.
imp.author: He had been rich for forty years and had buried two wives and one fortune, and he said to me, without turning, that the music sounded exactly as it had in eighteen ninety-nine, and that this was the saddest thing he knew.

imp.generic: We always think next year will be better even though it never is.
imp.author: We drive home along the dark coast road, each of us privately certain that next summer the lights will burn a little brighter, knowing in the same breath that they never do.

imp.generic: She danced with a rich, handsome guy and barely noticed me.
imp.author: She danced with a broad-shouldered boy from Yale who would inherit a railroad and a face that had never been refused anything, and when she passed me she smiled the smile she gave to waiters and to weather.
